chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about the one in Ihram who breaks his leg: 'What would be his state, and what is upon him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is free from Ihram, from everything.' I said: '(In terms of) women, clothes, and perfume?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, from the entirety of whatever is prohibited upon the one in Ihram.'

And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Has it not reached you the words of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): "Free me where you restricted me, by Your decree which You ordained upon me"?' I said: 'May Allah keep you well! What are you saying regarding Hajj?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He must perform Hajj the next year.'

I said: 'Inform me about the confined one (al-mahsur) and the prevented one (al-masdud). Are they equal?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No.' I said: 'So inform me about the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) when the Polytheists prevented him. Did he fulfill his Umra?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but he performed Umra after that.'

key_terms.الْمَحْصُورِ: The confined one (prevented from completing ritual due to injury or obstacle)
key_terms.الْمَصْدُودِ: The prevented one (prevented from entering Mecca or completing ritual due to external force)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj/Umra)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who breaks their leg or is prevented from completing Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the distinction between 'injury' (which dissolves Ihram restrictions like clothing and perfume) and 'obstruction' (which requires completing the ritual later), citing the Prophet’s (SAW) post-Hudaibiyyah Umra as a precedent for the latter. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the phrase 'Hullee haythu habasani' (Free me where you bound me) to justify the flexibility in expiation when external forces prevent Hajj completion.
